title: Raibach Design A2UI — Room catalog
whatThisFileIs: THE ROOM'S SCHEMA. What the room's server validates its payload against — an unknown component fails loud with HTTP 503. Derived from surface-design/registry.ts so the allowlist and the schema cannot disagree; catalog.json beside this file is the export the server loads.
description: Custom A2UI v0.9.1 catalog for the Design A2UI room. The room draws only the components named here: the frame and the left column's foot, derived from the room's registry, plus the primitive floor.

text.description: The text content to display. Simple Markdown supported (no HTML, images, or links).

variant.description: A hint for the base text style. 'greeting' is the Grace welcome-message style used at the top of assembled surfaces.

url.description: The URL of the image. Must be a registered catalog ID from the A2UI Image Catalog (raibach-logo, card-bg-design-system, card-img-default, molecule-logo).

description.description: Accessibility text for the image (WCAG 2.1 AA required).

allOf.description: A layout component that arranges its children horizontally.

children.description: Defines the children by ID reference. Use explicitList for fixed children or template for data-driven lists.

allOf.description: A layout component that arranges its children vertically.

children.description: Defines the children by ID reference.

child.description: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card.
The ID of the child component (typically a Text for the label).

allOf.description: THE CHAT SEAT: the right column, its five slots, the conversation and the turn.
THE CHAT TAB PAGE: the same seat as the Home sub-surface, reading the console package.
THE RAIL: the sub-surface navigation, the collapse control and the console mark.
THE CONVERSATIONS CARD AND THE RESPONSE CARD: the bar, the rows and the slot the thread sits in.
THE THREAD: the turns, their bubbles and their action links.
THE INPUT BAR: Send, Stop, the input grip and the trailing control.
THE INPUT REGION: the height the person drags and the slot the typing box sits in.
THE TYPING BOX: the value, its placeholder and its measured height.
THE FOOT: the tray the seat carries when the product room does not bind its own tools.
THE READOUT: the session, the usage and the status line above the thread.
THE FOLD: a disclosure for one list — the inspections, the trace — opened and closed.
THE SESSIONS VIEW: the stored-query rows, the receipt and the refusal.
THE BANNER: one refusal, said where the person is already reading.
THE DISCLOSURE: a label and the body it opens. Switched off in the top slot today.
THE PERSON TURN: the design's own row for what the person said.
THE PRODUCT FOOT: attach, tool and the connection flags the product room binds.
THE PRODUCT THREAD: the run's own turns, with its clock and the expected minutes.
THE WORK CARD: the clock, the stage trail and the shimmer while a turn is in flight.
THE ROOM: the frame and its five slots — left-header, left, left-footer, middle and right — and the grips that resize and collapse them.
THE CONSOLE GRID: the design packages, two rows at a time, paged to the pane it is drawn in. Each card is the room's own copy of the console card.
THE REPAIR LIST: the catalogue checker's findings, blocking first, with the marks a repair in flight writes.
THE LEFT COLUMN'S FOOT: the Save control, the next-session control and the host's own answer under them. It draws and dispatches; the seat that holds the session decides what saving means.
THE INGEST FORM: the Figma address, the notes and Submit.
THE CATALOGUE TREE: the measured layers, the filter and the catalogue head above them.
THE TOOLS TAB: the ingest form over the catalogue tree.

weight.description: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column (CSS flex-grow). Only valid for direct children of Row or Column.

primaryColor.description: Primary brand color in hex format.

iconUrl.description: URL for an image identifying the agent or tool.

agentDisplayName.description: Display name for the agent or tool that created the surface.
